A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Med-SegLens research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original latent-alignment, segmentation-intervention and transfer results, plus appendix ablations and CelebAMask-HQ examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds CT-ORG latent visualizations and U-Net transfer experiments.

M1.justification: The BatchTopK SAE, encoder/decoder Hungarian alignment, shared-latent criterion and additive/multiplicative interventions remain unchanged. Appendix F explicitly applies the existing pipeline to CT-ORG without algorithmic changes; suggested deployment tuning signals are not implemented method additions.

E1.justification: Appendix F adds training and qualitative evaluation on CT-ORG, substantially broadening medical coverage from brain MRI to multi-organ CT, including liver, bladder, kidneys, bone and lungs. IXI, all three BraTS populations and CelebAMask-HQ remain represented.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Greedy, Sinkhorn and encoder-only Hungarian alignment in Tables 2 and 8, and connected-component filtering and uncertainty filtering in Tables 3–5. The new U-Net study tests another backbone rather than adding a competing method.

E3.justification: Appendix G adds ALS/MLS evaluation on U-Net for both Adult/Pediatric transfer directions. Figure 17 sweeps steering strength from -5 to 5 and reports mean and edema Dice. Existing experiments retain their settings, including Section 7's SegFormer sweep from -100 to 100.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds an architecture-robustness check with steering-strength sensitivity curves for U-Net, testing whether intervention effects extend beyond SegFormer. Existing layer-selection, dictionary-size, feature-swapping and failure-mode analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: No new run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests are reported. Bootstrap-based alignment Stability and the existing distribution plots retain their reporting practices; the added U-Net curves introduce no uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Figures 15–17 add organ-associated CT latents and U-Net transfer curves showing beneficial steering ranges in both directions. Existing numerical results in Tables 1–8 and the earlier brain-MRI and facial-part findings remain unchanged. The additions concern new dataset/backbone settings.

T1.justification: The SAE equations, alignment definitions, feature-swapping formulation, steering equations and appendix geometry metrics are retained. Generalizing brain terminology to other structures introduces no new formal definition, derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same novelty, causal-bottleneck and retraining-free intervention claims, including approximately 70% failure recovery and Dice improvement from 39.4% to 74.2%. New experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: The new Discussion explicitly distinguishes analytical steering sweeps from deployment, where ground-truth Dice is unavailable, and suggests unevaluated label-free tuning signals. It also discusses single-layer limitations, possible multi-scale extensions and mask-based applicability across anatomy. Earlier conclusion limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository hyperlink in the abstract and documents SegFormer/Dice training with SAE sparsity 32 and expansion factor 16 for CT-ORG. Condensing CelebAMask-HQ documentation removes its explicit 512-by-512 annotation resolution; other principal implementation disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds the CT-ORG reference by Rister et al. and replaces the introductory Litjens et al. survey citation with Ahmed et al.'s J-RAS paper. The related-work argument and novelty positioning remain stable; other reference changes largely update bibliographic details.

P1.justification: v2 adds a Discussion, acknowledgements and Appendix G, and rewrites Appendix F as 'Beyond Brain MRI' while condensing its facial-dataset description. Publication and affiliation text also change. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds CT processing Figure 15 and U-Net Figure 17, combines new CT examples with the retained facial examples in Figure 16, and removes dataset-summary Table 9. Figure 2's caption clarifies architecture attribution, with limited figure/table relocation elsewhere.

improvement.justification: CT-ORG examples and U-Net transfer sweeps modestly strengthen applicability evidence, while the repository pointer and deployment discussion improve access information and transparency. These benefits outweigh the limited loss of CelebAMask-HQ detail. The gains remain bounded: CT validation is qualitative, suggested label-free steering selection is untested, and the core quantitative evidence is unchanged.
